themes_detail.label: Elevator Safety Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints in CD 404 spiked to 27 this week, a 232% increase from the 8.1-week average, suggesting widespread mechanical failures or maintenance failures affecting resident mobility and accessibility in multi-unit buildings.
evidence: 27 elevator complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 8.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (232% spike, z-score: 5.86)
Statistically significant deviation indicating acute, not chronic, problem
Elmhurst/South Corona has dense multi-unit residential stock where elevator failure creates accessibility crisis for elderly and disabled residents
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings with failed elevators; identify which buildings are repeat offenders and whether landlords are negligent
Check DOB violation records for these buildings — are elevators failing inspection? Are fines being levied and ignored?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 7 this week, a 600% spike from the 1.0-week average, suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown or illicit vending activity surge in the district.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (600% spike, z-score: 5.37)
Timing suggests either coordinated enforcement action or new vending problem requiring intervention
CD 404 has robust street commerce; shift could reflect policy change or community pressure
reporting_angles: Did NYPD or Dept of Consumer Affairs initiate enforcement sweep? Interview street vendors about new restrictions or harassment
Are complaints coming from residents about illegal vendors, or from vendors about overreach? Whose perspective dominates?

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints hit 3 last week, a 2300% spike from the 0.1-week baseline average, indicating possible sudden arboriculture crisis or environmental stress event affecting the district's canopy.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating most statistically anomalous deviation
Could signal disease, pest outbreak, drought stress, or recent infrastructure damage (construction, utility work)
reporting_angles: Was there recent utility work, construction, or extreme weather? Investigate environmental trigger
Contact NYC Parks to determine if there's a documented disease or pest issue affecting trees in this district

themes_detail.label: SPIT Inspections Spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped to 4 this week, a 700% increase from the 0.5-week average, suggesting heightened building code enforcement or possible tenant harassment through aggressive inspections.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
SPIT is NYC DOB's specialized enforcement unit for multi-unit buildings — complaints suggest aggressive enforcement or tenant concerns about overreach
Timing aligns with broader inspection activity signal (GENERAL complaints also up 172% last week)
reporting_angles: Are tenants being cited for code violations? Interview residents about what sparked SPIT visits and outcomes
Is this coordinated enforcement targeting specific buildings or neighborhoods? Cross-reference with DOB permit data

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Missing and dangling street sign complaints (combined 6 complaints over past 3 weeks) represent a 600% average spike from baseline, indicating deferred maintenance or vandalism affecting wayfinding and pedestrian safety.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Street Sign - Missing: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Combined pattern suggests systemic street furniture maintenance failure rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Has DOT deferred street sign maintenance budget? Check capital project schedules for CD 404
Are specific corridors more affected? This could indicate geographic equity issue in service delivery
